To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the saturated solubilities of bone mineral are elevated by the action of one or more non-collagenous proteins and that parathyroid hormone increases the saturated solubibility of hydroxyapatites by increasing the concentration of the protein(s) that elevate(s) the solubility.

the concentration of calcium in plasma is determined by a combination of the saturated solubilities of noncollagen proteins and hydroxyaptite and that the concentration of free calcium is controlled by the parathyroid gland.
the concentration of free calcium is set by the noncollagenous protein matrix of the bone surface and the saturated solubilities of the hydroxyapatite crystals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of extracellular proteins in the control of calcium concentrations of body fluids.
the role of the extracellular environment in the maintenance of plasma calcium concentration.
the role of the noncollagenous protein, osteocalcin, in calcium control in extracellular fluid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the extracellular calcium concentration is determined by the saturated solubilities of noncollagen proteins and hydroxyapaptite and that the parathyroid hormone acts to increase the saturated solubilization of the noncollagenous protein.
the solubility product of calcium hydroxyapatite in the presence of noncollagenus proteins and other extracellular factors is a function of the extracellular fluid calcium concentration.

the solubility characteristics of bone mineral surfaces are controlled by noncollagenous extracellular proteins and that the concentration of calcium in body fluids is determined by the solubility properties of the bone mineral.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium homeostasis is not a function of the skeleton, but a process that controls the skeleton.
plasma calcium is undersaturated with respect to hydroxyapatite but supersaturated with respect to noncollagenous protein.
plasma calcium concentration is set by the saturated solubilities of noncollagen proteins and hydroxyapytite and not by the action of the parathyroid hormone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium is not a free ion in the extracellular space but is bound to proteins and that the bound ion has a different solubility than the unbound ion.
the solubility control of calcium in body fluids is the most important factor in calcium homeostasis and is a key factor in the control of the bone mineral phase of bone metabolism.
the concentration of calcium in body fluids is controlled not only by noncollagenous bone proteins, but also by the parathyroid hormone.
